root_cause.text: The vt subsystem fails to discard the stale saved unicode screen buffer (`vc_saved_uni_lines`) after a console resize while in the alternate screen, causing out-of-bounds memory access when the buffer is restored and accessed with mismatched dimensions.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and patch explain that `enter_alt_screen()` saves `vc_uni_lines` into `vc_saved_uni_lines` and sets `vc_uni_lines` to NULL. A subsequent `vc_do_resize()` skips reallocating the unicode buffer because `vc_uni_lines` is NULL, but `vc_saved_uni_lines` retains the old buffer allocated for original dimensions. When `leave_alt_screen()` later restores `vc_saved_uni_lines`, the buffer dimensions no longer match `vc_rows/vc_cols`, leading to out-of-bounds reads (e.g., in `csi_J`). The fix adds a check on dimension changes before restoring and frees the stale buffer if mismatched.

vuln_statements.explanation: Restores the unicode screen buffer from the saved pointer without any size check. If the saved buffer was allocated with different dimensions (due to a resize while in alternate screen), subsequent accesses to the unicode screen will read/write out of bounds, directly causing the vulnerability.

Clears the saved unicode buffer pointer only after the unchecked restore. This does not prevent the out-of-bounds access that already occurred on the previous line. The buffer should have been freed or rechecked before restoration.

Awareness of dimension mismatch is shown for the text screen rows, but no analogous clamp or check is applied to the unicode buffer. This omission means the unicode buffer can be restored with dimensions that exceed the current console size, leading to out-of-bounds access.

Same as rows: provides safe access for the text screen using clamped columns, but the unicode buffer lacks similar protection. This allows the unicode buffer to be restored with mismatched sizes, enabling out-of-bounds read/write.

This check only verifies the existence of the saved text screen (vc_saved_screen) before proceeding with restoration. It does not check whether the saved unicode buffer (vc_saved_uni_lines) is stale or correctly sized, allowing the vulnerable restoration path to continue with mismatched dimensions.

Early returns the function if no saved text screen exists, but does not handle the case where vc_saved_uni_lines is still set (stale from a previous alternate screen). This can leave a stale unicode buffer that may be restored later without validation.

This memcpy for the text screen uses the safe clamped cols, highlighting that safe copying is performed for the text buffer while no equivalent safe copying or allocation exists for the unicode buffer. The contrast shows the missing protection for the unicode data.
